text: Given the caller passes graph_send_mail 1 valid attachment (filename + optional type + base64 content, decoded <=500KB), When the tool is called, Then the request body sent to Graph has message.attachments with 1 item, and name/contentType/contentBytes match the input verbatim

Given attachments contains 5 valid attachments (each decoded <=500KB, total <=700KB), When called, Then message.attachments contains all 5 items, and each item's name/contentType/contentBytes matches the corresponding input

Given attachments is not passed (parameter omitted, or explicitly null/empty list), When called, Then the request body sent to Graph has no attachments key, byte-for-byte identical to before the change

Given an attachment's content_base64 is not valid base64, When called, Then an invalid_argument error is returned whose message names which filename, and the fake client's recorded HTTP call list is empty (no request was made)

Given a single attachment decodes to 500,001 bytes (1 byte over the 500KB per-file limit), When called, Then an invalid_argument error is returned stating the per-file limit was exceeded, and no HTTP request is made
Given attachments contains 6 attachments (over the 5-attachment count limit), When called, Then an invalid_argument error is returned stating the count limit was exceeded, and no HTTP request is made

Given a single attachment decodes to exactly 500,000 bytes (equal to the limit, boundary value), When called, Then validation passes and the request is sent to Graph normally (verifying the boundary check uses greater-than rather than greater-or-equal)
Given one item in attachments is missing the filename field, When called, Then an invalid_argument error is returned whose message names the missing field as filename, and no HTTP request is made

Given graph_send_mail is called twice in a row, each with a different fake client (different token/mailbox context) and different attachment contents, When called in sequence, Then the request body sent to Graph by the second call does not contain the first call's attachment content, and the two results leave nothing behind (verifies the tool has no mutable state shared across requests)

Given 2 attachments of 350,001 bytes each (each <=500KB, total 700,002 bytes exceeds the 700KB total limit), When called, Then an invalid_argument error is returned stating the total limit was exceeded, and no HTTP request is made
